# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of LiteSDCard: the PHY, the core, the two DMAs and the
events. It is generated from the register definitions of the gateware, elaborated without
an FPGA toolchain on the standalone core that `litesdcard_gen` builds, with 4 and with 8
data lines.

A LiteX SoC places every register of LiteSDCard in one bank named after the
module, `sdcard` with `add_sdcard()`. This appendix splits it by block: each table lists
the registers whose names start with its prefix, so `card_detect` in the table of
`sdcard_phy` is `sdcard_phy_card_detect` in `csr.csv`. Offsets are in bytes from the base
of the `sdcard` bank; the base address depends on the SoC and is in the `csr.csv` of a
build.

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `gen_4bit` | `litesdcard_gen` `--vendor lattice` `--clk-freq 100e6` `--dma-data-width 32` `4 data lines` |
| `gen_8bit` | `litesdcard_gen` `--vendor lattice` `--clk-freq 100e6` `--dma-data-width 32` `8 data lines (data subsignal widened)` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`, or a `CSRStatus` that
software also writes, such as event pending bits cleared by writing 1), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `CSRStorage`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. The BIOS driver uses these names through the generated `csr.h`, and the Linux driver
finds the blocks through the device tree, so neither needs the offsets.

## PHY {#reg-sdcard-phy}

Defined by `SDPHY` (`litesdcard/phy.py`).

The three timeouts count system clock cycles. `add_sdcard` builds the PHY with 1 s for the
response and read timeouts (`cmd_timeout=10e-1`, `data_timeout=10e-1`), so their reset
value is the system clock frequency, `0x5f5e100` at 100 MHz; their class defaults are
10 ms. It leaves the write timeout at its class default, 500 ms (`write_timeout=500e-3`),
`0x2faf080` at 100 MHz. A write timeout ends the block and sets `data_event.timeout`.

The bits of `dataw_status` are cleared when a write
starts and set by the token of each block, so they sum up the whole last write.

`settings` resets to 4-bit; the BIOS writes 1-bit before the initialization and widens the
bus once the card supports it. The 8-bit design has the same registers: with 8 data lines
the PHY only adds the constant `sdcard_phy_support_8x` (1) to `csr.csv`, which `soc.h`
exports as `SDCARD_PHY_SUPPORT_8X` ([PHY: clocking and IO](#phy)).

Bank `sdcard_phy`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `card_detect` | `0x0000` | 1 | ro | Level of the card detect pad `cd` (0 when the pads have none). The BIOS reads 1 as no card. |
| `clocker_divider` | `0x0004` | 9 | rw | Card clock divider: the card clock is the system clock divided by `divider` rounded up to even, and by 2 at least. Reset `0x100`. |
| `init_initialize` | `0x0008` | 1 | wo | Write: send the power-up clocks, 80 card clocks with CMD and DAT high; when the pads have `rst`, they follow a card reset as long as 4096 card clock periods, with the clock stopped. |
| `cmdr_timeout` | `0x000c` | 32 | rw | Response timeout in system clock cycles: wait for the start bit, the response bytes and the busy of an R1b. Reset `0x5f5e100`. |
| `dataw_status` | `0x0010` | 3 | ro | CRC status tokens of the last write. See the fields below. |
| `dataw_timeout` | `0x0014` | 32 | rw | Write timeout in system clock cycles, for each block of a write: wait for the CRC status token and the end of the busy. Reset `0x2faf080`. |
| `datar_timeout` | `0x0018` | 32 | rw | Read timeout in system clock cycles, for each block of a read; it does not count while the PHY stops the card clock for back-pressure. Reset `0x5f5e100`. |
| `settings` | `0x001c` | 2 | rw | Bus width of the data transfers: `0b00` 1-bit, `0b01` 4-bit, `0b10` 8-bit. Reset `0x1`. |

Fields of `dataw_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `accepted` | 0 | 1: the card accepted a block (token `010`). |
| `crc_error` | 1 | 1: the card reported a CRC error on a block (token `101`). |
| `write_error` | 2 | 1: the card reported a write error on a block (token `110`). |

## Core {#reg-sdcard-core}

Defined by `SDCore` (`litesdcard/core.py`).

`cmd_command` takes the response type in `cmd_type` (0 none, 1 short, 2 long, 3 short with
busy), the data direction in `data_type` (0 none, 1 read, 2 write) and the command index in
`cmd`. Writing `cmd_send` starts the command and its data transfer, and clears both event
registers; their `done` bits read 1 again when the core is idle.

`cmd_response` holds the
response right-aligned: for a short response, the first five bytes (the 32-bit payload in
bits 31:0, without the CRC byte); for a long one, the 16 bytes after the first.

In `cmd_event`, a response timeout sets `timeout` and `error`, and a CRC7 mismatch, when
`cmd_command.crc` is 1, sets `crc` and `error`; for a data command, both also set
`data_event.error`, since the data phase is skipped. In `data_event`, `timeout` reports a
read or write timeout, `crc` a CRC16 error on a read or a `101` token on a write, and
`error` the other rejected tokens of a write ([Core: commands, responses, CRC](#core)).

Bank `sdcard_core`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `cmd_argument` | `0x0020` | 32 | rw | SDCard Cmd Argument. Reset `0x0`. |
| `cmd_command` | `0x0024` | 14 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `cmd_send` | `0x0028` | 1 | rw | Run Cmd/Data transfer. Reset `0x0`. |
| `cmd_response` | `0x002c` | 128 | ro | SDCard Cmd Response. |
| `cmd_event` | `0x003c` | 4 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `data_event` | `0x0040` | 4 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `block_length` | `0x0044` | 10 | rw | Data transfer Block Length (in bytes). Reset `0x0`. |
| `block_count` | `0x0048` | 32 | rw | Data transfer Block Count. Reset `0x0`. |

Fields of `cmd_command`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `cmd_type` | 1:0 | Core/PHY Cmd transfer type. |
| `crc` | 2 | Enable CRC7 check for response. |
| `data_type` | 6:5 | Core/PHY Data transfer type. |
| `cmd` | 13:8 | SDCard Cmd. |

Fields of `cmd_event`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `done` | 0 | Cmd transfer has been executed. |
| `error` | 1 | Cmd transfer has failed due to error(s). |
| `timeout` | 2 | Timeout error. |
| `crc` | 3 | CRC Error. |

Fields of `data_event`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `done` | 0 | Data transfer has been executed. |
| `error` | 1 | Data transfer has failed due to error(s). |
| `timeout` | 2 | Timeout Error. |
| `crc` | 3 | CRC Error. |

## Block2mem DMA {#reg-sdcard-block2mem}

Defined by `SDBlock2MemDMA` (`litesdcard/frontend/dma.py`).

The registers come from the LiteX `WishboneDMAWriter`, which the descriptions call the DMA
Writer: it writes the blocks read from the card into memory. `base` and `length` are in
bytes and must be multiples of the bus width in bytes, else the DMA stops at once with
`error`; `offset` counts bus words.

Writing 0 to `enable` resets the DMA, `done` and `error`
included. The DMA takes the data of a read only when `enable` is 1 before the first byte
arrives: set it before the command ([DMAs](#dma)).

Bank `sdcard_block2mem`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `dma_base` | `0x004c` | 64 | rw | DMA Writer base address. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_length` | `0x0054` | 32 | rw | DMA Writer transfer length in bytes. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_enable` | `0x0058` | 1 | rw | DMA Writer enable. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_done` | `0x005c` | 1 | ro | DMA Writer transfer done. |
| `dma_loop` | `0x0060` | 1 | rw | DMA Writer loop enable. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_offset` | `0x0064` | 32 | ro | DMA Writer current transfer offset. |
| `dma_error` | `0x0068` | 1 | ro | DMA Writer rejected a non-word-aligned base or length. Cleared when disabled. |

## Mem2block DMA {#reg-sdcard-mem2block}

Defined by `SDMem2BlockDMA` (`litesdcard/frontend/dma.py`).

The registers come from the LiteX `WishboneDMAReader`, which the descriptions call the DMA
Reader: it reads from memory the blocks to write to the card. `base`, `length`, `offset` and
`enable` behave as in block2mem ([DMAs](#dma)).

Bank `sdcard_mem2block`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `dma_base` | `0x006c` | 64 | rw | DMA Reader base address. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_length` | `0x0074` | 32 | rw | DMA Reader transfer length in bytes. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_enable` | `0x0078` | 1 | rw | DMA Reader enable. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_done` | `0x007c` | 1 | ro | DMA Reader transfer done. |
| `dma_loop` | `0x0080` | 1 | rw | DMA Reader loop enable. Reset `0x0`. |
| `dma_offset` | `0x0084` | 32 | ro | DMA Reader current transfer offset. |
| `dma_error` | `0x0088` | 1 | ro | DMA Reader rejected a non-word-aligned base or length. Cleared when disabled. |

## Events and interrupt {#reg-sdcard-ev}

Defined by `add_sdcard` (`litex/soc/integration/soc.py`).

`add_sdcard`, a method of the LiteX SoC, adds an `EventManager` with five sources:
`card_detect`, `block2mem_dma`
and `mem2block_dma` are pulses, cleared by writing 1 to their `pending` bit; `data_done`
and `cmd_done` are levels that follow the `done` bits of the core events.

The interrupt of the event manager
goes to the interrupt controller of the SoC when the SoC has one, and to the `irq` pin of
`litesdcard_gen`. A design built with `mode="read"` or `mode="write"` has one DMA and
its event only: the registers of the other DMA are absent, the offsets after them move
down, and the bits of the event sources after the missing one move down by one.

Bank `sdcard_ev`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `status` | `0x008c` | 5 | ro | This register contains the current raw level of the event trigger. Writes to this register have no effect. |
| `pending` | `0x0090` | 5 | rw | When an event occurs, the corresponding bit will be set in this register. To clear the Event, set the corresponding bit in this register. |
| `enable` | `0x0094` | 5 | rw | This register enables the corresponding events. Write a ``0`` to this register to disable individual events. Reset `0x0`. |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `card_detect` | 0 | Level of the ``card_detect`` event. |
| `block2mem_dma` | 1 | Level of the ``block2mem_dma`` event. |
| `mem2block_dma` | 2 | Level of the ``mem2block_dma`` event. |
| `data_done` | 3 | Level of the ``data_done`` event. |
| `cmd_done` | 4 | Level of the ``cmd_done`` event. |

Fields of `pending`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `card_detect` | 0 | SDCard has been ejected/inserted. |
| `block2mem_dma` | 1 | Block2Mem DMA terminated. |
| `mem2block_dma` | 2 | Mem2Block DMA terminated. |
| `data_done` | 3 | Transfer completed (cmd and data). |
| `cmd_done` | 4 | Command completed. |

Fields of `enable`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `card_detect` | 0 | Write a ``1`` to enable the ``card_detect`` Event. |
| `block2mem_dma` | 1 | Write a ``1`` to enable the ``block2mem_dma`` Event. |
| `mem2block_dma` | 2 | Write a ``1`` to enable the ``mem2block_dma`` Event. |
| `data_done` | 3 | Write a ``1`` to enable the ``data_done`` Event. |
| `cmd_done` | 4 | Write a ``1`` to enable the ``cmd_done`` Event. |
